- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast spikes; correct by adding 10–30% to forecasted values for high-sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) and model shows sharp upward spikes, model over-estimates; cap upward forecasts at 1.5x the 14-day moving average.
- Model consistently under-estimates true outcomes in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a 15–25% upward bias for this window.
- After a strong sentiment spike (e.g., sentiment >0.67 for 3+ consecutive days), model often over-responds; reduce forecast by 15–25% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model shows mean-reversion bias: if recent 7-day average is >1.80, forecast tends to drop; if <1.60, tends to rise — adjust by aligning with 7-day moving average ±0.10.
- For sentiment history with alternating +/– signals, model often mis-weights volatility; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3 days to adjust forecast volatility.
